title: Identify the code imported by the benchmark process
applies_when: Python benchmarks involve editable installs, multiple checkouts, generated modules, native extensions or a long-lived interpreter that may retain an earlier import; a single-module screen rejects relative imports requiring package context, or an installed optional shim conflicts with exact source; test claims depend on parametrized backend selection through Hypothesis wrappers, including bound test methods, or mocked dependency bindings; validation tools differ from the repository's pinned version; supposedly isolated native tests use fixed host endpoints or persistent fixtures.
lesson: Use the actual benchmark interpreter and environment to inspect module origins, including __file__ or __spec__.origin where available. Check the callable's defining module and the native extension build when relevant. Python's module cache and import search path can make an edited checkout differ from the code being measured; use a fresh process when cached imports obscure the comparison. File-scoped test dependencies need not cover the full suite. Record resolved packages and compare the same tests and failure details on unchanged baseline and candidate before attributing a failure to the patch. Patch a mock at the binding the consumer actually reads, not a similarly named defining-module alias. Verify the replacement was reached and retain normal/error-path controls; replacing unrelated imports does not establish native package or integration correctness. Separate processes do not isolate fixed host ports: serialize such native test arms or use genuinely separate network namespaces. A fresh address, working directory or TMPDIR also does not isolate a hard-coded absolute fixture: JuiceFS memkv reads /tmp/juicefs.memkv.setting.json regardless of the supplied address. Inspect backend initialization before claiming a clean test; use an actually task-private backend or filesystem namespace, never clear another workload's fixture. A test parameter label is not proof of the realized backend: when it supports a cross-backend claim, assert the actual runtime selection inside the test body and use reversed-order/fresh-process controls if a wrapper may retain the first runner. A normal result assertion can pass while the second backend silently repeats the first. Include both function and bound-method forms when changing wrapper state: saving an attribute on a function can work while assigning it to a bound method raises AttributeError. AnyIO 4.15.1 with parametrized Hypothesis tests is one concrete counterexample, not evidence that ordinary parametrization is generally broken.
avoid_when: A matching Python filename does not prove that a compiled extension or captured graph contains the new code. Namespace and built-in modules may have no ordinary source file. Import checks can execute module initialization, so choose a safe diagnostic entry point. A single-module package-context rejection is a screen limitation, not NO_BUG or permission to execute a full checkout. After owner review, use separate full-source roots and fresh processes for matched native tests; inspect optional dependency origins too. A real same-commit pure-Python shim may resolve an installed-shim mismatch without mocks or global installation, but only when its provenance and applicable API match. Check package namespaces exactly (name == 'flashinfer' or name.startswith('flashinfer.')); a loose prefix also captures distinct distributions such as flashinfer_cubin. Source-root selection does not prove their ABI compatibility. A shared failure name alone does not establish identical cause or make either arm fully qualified; retain details and consider nondeterminism or interactions. Check validation-tool --version and the exact repository pin/config before changing code for a new lint diagnostic; compare unchanged baseline and candidate with the same tool. A newer Ruff warning is not by itself a patch regression, but a warning is not harmless merely because it is old. Do not silently ignore rules or claim full repository checks from two-file lint/format. A task-private venv is not an untrusted-code sandbox.

evidence.note: The PR records matched full-source, fresh-process native FP8-preparation tests using the same-commit JIT-cache shim: baseline 3 failed/2 passed, candidate 5 passed. This is focused invalid-argument correctness evidence, not full-suite, fused-kernel, performance, merge or prospective Scout-improvement evidence. A single-module relative-import block did not establish absence of the bug.

This pinned source declares ruff==0.14.10 for quality checks. It supports checking the validation-tool version as part of execution identity, not an unpublished bug, local pass, full repository qualification or proof that all newer diagnostics are spurious.

Python documents patching where an object is looked up rather than necessarily where it is defined. This is a test-boundary mechanism, not evidence that a mocked component run validates a full package.

The reported Hypothesis wrapper retains its first runner across parametrized backends. Check execution identity, not pytest's backend suffix. Existing PR #1354 addresses this issue; this lesson is not an independent approval of that fix.

Maintainer review explains why the proposed runner rewrap fixes ordinary functions but breaks bound test methods, and requests a class-method regression. Do not equate one repaired dispatch form with complete wrapper qualification. The review is public mechanism evidence, not acceptance of the current PR or a measured improvement to Scout.
The Python reference documents the module cache, search path and module specifications. These mechanisms explain source ambiguity; it does not validate any local installation or build.

The native suite requires chardet, CLI/decoder extras and test tools beyond HTTPX's minimum runtime or focused URL environment. Tooling pins do not pin every runtime dependency; record resolution rather than assuming identical environments.

The official test instructions warn that suite servers use fixed ports 8000 and 8001. Independent Python processes on one host do not reserve independent endpoints. This supports a scheduling caution, not a measured throughput or general sandbox claim.

newMockClient reads a fixed absolute settingPath and does not use addr for fixture isolation. This source establishes the persistence mechanism, not a clean memkv run, a production defect or a measured Scout improvement. A fresh process, URI or TMPDIR alone cannot isolate that file.
